source: Wikipedia: Strategic planning (evidence section)
finding: The page's evidence section rests on one 2019 meta-analysis (George, Walker, Monster). Planning has a positive effect on performance, strongest for effectiveness (reaching goals). A bare plan is not enough: it needs formality, comprehensiveness and stakeholder management.
numbers: Meta-analysis of 'almost 9,000 public and private organizations'; no effect size on the page.
quote: strategic planning is found to have a positive impact on organizational performance.
limits: Secondary source; no r value. Defines comprehensiveness as 'producing many strategic options before selecting the course to follow'.
agent_relevance: Option generation (many options before selection) is named as one of three conditions. Supports a Generate step, but only as a moderator claim, not a tested one.

source: Wikipedia: Strategic planning (History section) citing McKinsey Quarterly 2006 'Improving Strategic Planning'
finding: McKinsey survey (2006): many firms had a formal planning process, but it was not used for their most important decisions.
numbers: No respondent count or percentages on the Wikipedia page.
quote: the process was not being used for their most important decisions
limits: The McKinsey page itself timed out twice; numbers not verified. Self-report survey.
agent_relevance: A scaffold that exists but is bypassed on high-stakes items is a known failure. Route the hardest items through the schema, not only the easy ones.

source: Shea-Van Fossen, Rothstein, Korn (2006) Thirty-five years of strategic planning and firm performance research: a meta-analysis (AOM Annual Meeting)
finding: Pooled effect is positive, but it shrinks to near zero once publication bias is corrected by trim and fill.
numbers: 39 studies, 74 independent effect sizes, 5,223 firms. Standardised mean difference 0.257 (p<.001). After trim and fill: 0.109, CI (-0.235, 0.242), which includes zero. Moderators tested: financial measure, planning definition, firm size, measurement period, data type.
limits: Conference abstract page only; full paper not read. Effect is not robust to publication bias.
agent_relevance: Warns that 'planning works' may be inflated. Any schema claim about planning gains needs a held-out test (G3).

source: Wikipedia: Henry Mintzberg
finding: Mintzberg (1994, The Rise and Fall of Strategic Planning) calls 'strategic planning' an oxymoron. He favours emergent strategy (patterns arising informally) over deliberate strategy.
limits: Secondary summary; no empirical numbers.
agent_relevance: Main opposing theory. Emergent strategy maps to revising from real output (G2) rather than committing to a plan up front.

source: Wikipedia: Strategic management (Ansoff, Mintzberg, Chaffee, Woodhouse and Collingridge)
finding: Ansoff (1965) built gap analysis: measure the distance between present state and goal, then pick gap-reducing actions. Mintzberg (1988) says realised strategy can differ from intended, and the difference is emergent. Chaffee (1985) agrees. Woodhouse and Collingridge: being strategic means intelligent trial and error.
numbers: By 1979 an estimated 45% of Fortune 500 firms used some form of growth-share matrix in planning. Only first 100,000 of 210,931 characters were read.
limits: PIMS section not read. No performance effect sizes in the part read.
agent_relevance: Gap analysis is close to our goal-versus-state check. The trial-and-error view matches test-then-revise.

source: Wikipedia: Business plan
finding: The page has no studies on planning and performance. It notes plans often underestimate costs and overestimate revenue, and mentions reference class forecasting as a fix.
limits: Maintenance notices on the page (original research, missing citations). Practitioner opinion only.
agent_relevance: Optimistic forecasts in plans are a known bias; a reference-class check is a possible code-side guard.

source: Boyd (1991) Strategic planning and financial performance: a meta-analytic review. J Management Studies 28(4)
finding: Early meta-analysis. Studies disagreed (benefit, none, small negative) and used small samples. Pooling gave modest positive correlations with nine performance measures. The author argues measurement problems mean the true link is understated.
limits: Abstract read via Crossref only; r values not read. The 'underestimate' claim is the author's argument.
agent_relevance: Baseline: small positive effect, noisy measures.

source: Schwenk and Shrader (1993) Effects of formal strategic planning on financial performance in small firms: a meta-analysis. Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice
finding: First meta-analysis for small firms. Effect per study is small but overall positive and significant. Most variance across studies is NOT explained by sampling error, so moderators exist. Conclusion: planning is beneficial for small firms.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Heterogeneity means the effect depends on context; one fixed recipe is risky.

source: Miller and Cardinal (1994) Strategic planning and firm performance: a synthesis of more than two decades of research. Academy of Management Journal 37(6):1649-1665
finding: Meta-analysis of 26 studies. Planning positively affects performance. Substantive contingency factors had little effect. Differences in method explain much of the inconsistency across earlier studies.
limits: From search-result snippets, not the paper. Later critics cite informant bias and publication bias.
agent_relevance: Suggests the planning effect is general, not niche. Weak evidence, consistent direction.

source: George, Walker and Monster (2019) Does strategic planning improve organizational performance? A meta-analysis. Public Administration Review 79(6):810-819
finding: Random-effects meta-analysis finds a positive, moderate, significant effect. Meta-regression: strongest when performance is effectiveness and when planning is formal. Holds in public and private sectors and in US and non-US samples.
numbers: 87 correlations from 31 empirical studies. Exact pooled r not read. Wikipedia describes 'almost 9,000' organisations.
quote: strategic planning has a positive, moderate, and significant impact on organizational performance.
limits: Crossref abstract only (paper is CC BY but the Wiley PDF is behind a bot check). The comprehensiveness and stakeholder conditions come from Wikipedia's summary, not from the abstract.
agent_relevance: Most recent meta-analysis; source of the 'many options' moderator for our Generate step.

source: Brinckmann, Grichnik and Kapsa (2010) Should entrepreneurs plan or just storm the castle? J Business Venturing 25(1)
finding: Meta-analysis of the planning-performance link in small firms, focused on contextual moderators. Cited 769 times (Semantic Scholar). Abstract withheld by publisher; results not read.
limits: Paywalled; Crossref and Semantic Scholar had no abstract. Any recollection of its pooled effect is unverified and not recorded here.
agent_relevance: Contextual moderators matter: do not assume planning helps equally on all item types.

source: Delmar and Shane (2003) Does business planning facilitate the development of new ventures? Strategic Management Journal 24(12)
finding: Planning is an early step that helps founders decide, balance resource supply and demand, and turn abstract goals into concrete operational steps. Planned ventures were less likely to disband and faster in product development and organizing.
numbers: 223 new Swedish ventures started in the first 9 months of 1998 (random sample).
limits: Abstract only. Observational; founders self-select into planning; coefficients not read.
agent_relevance: Mechanism: planning turns abstract goals into operational steps, similar to decomposition.

source: Song, Im, van der Bij and Song (2011) Does strategic planning enhance or impede innovation and firm performance? J Product Innovation Management
finding: Tests whether planning helps or hurts innovation as well as performance. Abstract not retrieved, so no result recorded.
limits: Metadata only.
agent_relevance: Question to carry to other angles: can planning suppress novelty?

source: Rudd, Greenley, Beatson and Lings (2008) Strategic planning and performance: extending the debate. J Business Research 61(2)
finding: Extends the planning-performance debate (cited 279 times per Semantic Scholar). Abstract unavailable.
limits: Metadata only.

source: Fredrickson and Mitchell (1984) Strategic decision processes: comprehensiveness and performance in an industry with an unstable environment. Academy of Management Journal 27(2)
finding: Founding test of comprehensive (rational) decision process in an unstable industry. Title shows the boundary condition under test (instability). Result not read; do not cite a direction until checked.
limits: Metadata only.
agent_relevance: Candidate boundary condition: option breadth and planning may behave differently when the environment shifts fast. Check before use.

source: Dean and Sharfman (1996) Does decision process matter? A study of strategic decision-making effectiveness. Academy of Management Journal 39(2)
finding: Tests whether process affects decision effectiveness. Result not read.
limits: Metadata only.
agent_relevance: Candidate evidence on analysis-before-choice. Check before use.

source: Fredrickson (1984) The comprehensiveness of strategic decision processes: extension, observations, future directions. Academy of Management Journal 27(3)
finding: Companion study to Fredrickson and Mitchell. Metadata only; contents not read.
limits: Metadata only.

source: Capon, Farley and Hulbert (1994) Strategic planning and financial performance: more evidence. J Management Studies
finding: Named in this literature as a further study. Lookup failed (HTTP 429), so no content.
limits: Not retrieved.

source: Pearce, Freeman and Robinson (1987) The tenuous link between formal strategic planning and financial performance. Academy of Management Review
finding: Title says the link is tenuous. Lookup failed; contents not read.
limits: Title only.

source: Ansoff (1965) Corporate Strategy and Mintzberg (1994) The Rise and Fall of Strategic Planning
finding: The two poles of the theory. Ansoff: systematic analytic planning prepares for the future. Mintzberg: planning rarely produces strategy; strategy emerges and plans can freeze it. Read only through Wikipedia (see a04, a05).
limits: Books not opened.
agent_relevance: Design choice: plan up front versus revise from output (G2). Both are in the schema.

source: Synthesis: no formal model found (inference from a01, a03, a08, a10)
finding: No formal or computational model of planning and performance was found. The literature is correlational meta-analysis. Offered mechanisms are decision quality, resource balancing and concrete steps; the opposing view is emergent strategy.
limits: Inference by this agent from the lines above, not a sourced claim.
agent_relevance: A direct test is possible: S3 with few versus many options on held-out items, as SUBFIELDS.md asks.
